extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants / practitioners preparing or correcting patent drawings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance from MPEP § 608.02 about the required content, format, acceptability, correction, filing, storage, and examiner handling of drawings (utility, plant, and design) in U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for color drawings/photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition may be filed when an application contains color photographs or color drawings as the drawings required by 37 CFR 1.81; anticipated grant only when a color drawing or color photograph is the only practical medium to disclose the subject matter in a printed utility patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this form paragraph in design applications. A decision to grant the petition is not an indication that color drawings are necessary to comply with statutory requirements. It is desirable to file any desired color drawings or photographs as part of the original application papers to avoid issues concerning statutory defects (e.g., lack of enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112 or new matter under 35 U.S.C. 132). See MPEP § 608.02(c) for location information in IFW applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of graphic drawing symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.84(n) permits graphic drawing symbols and other labeled representations for conventional elements where appropriate, subject to Office approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANSI and ISO publications may be used as guides and are generally acceptable, but the Office will not approve any published collection of symbols as a group — clarity must be decided case-by-case. Avoid overly specific symbols; label symbols with unclear meanings for clarification. In design patents, use symbols judiciously because they may interfere with a clear showing of the design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols to indicate materials when material is important
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific graphic symbols should be used to indicate various materials where the material is an important feature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conventional features/symbols to assist prior art searches. (MPEP indicates a list of such symbols.) Consider using color drawings in design applications instead of symbols to represent color (see MPEP § 1503.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must be acceptable (readable/reproducible) for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are accepted by OPAP if the drawings are readable and reproducible for publication purposes; drawings are either acceptable or unacceptable (no formal/informal distinction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should review drawings for disclosure of the claimed invention and proper use of reference numerals. Objections to drawings in utility or plant applications will not be held in abeyance unless applicant is otherwise notified in an Office action (37 CFR 1.85(a)). Correct drawing corrections should be made promptly before allowance to avoid delays or reductions to term adjustment (37 CFR 1.704(c)(10)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file corrected drawings upon notice
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP will send a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers if drawings are unacceptable for purposes of publication, giving applicant two months to file acceptable drawings (extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will not release applications to Technology Centers until acceptable drawings are filed. If corrections are necessary, new corrected drawings must be submitted within the time set by the Office; the Office will not release drawings for purposes of correction. If a corrected drawing is required at allowability, Office may set a three-month unextendable period to file corrected drawing to avoid abandonment (37 CFR 1.85(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiner should require immediate corrected drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If at assignment or when the application is taken up an examiner believes drawings do not permit reasonable examination, applicant should be required to immediately submit corrected drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings permit reasonable examination but are of such character as to render the application defective under 35 U.S.C. 112, examination should begin immediately with a requirement for corrected drawings and a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling drawings labeled 'informal'
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant indicates drawings as 'informal' but OPAP considers them acceptable, the examiner should not require replacement; if examiner objects, require correction in reply and do not hold the objection in abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.02(b), (d)-(h), (p) for specific grounds and procedures regarding drawing informalities and objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely filed drawings lead to abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a drawing is not timely received in reply to a notice from the Office or a letter from the examiner requiring a drawing, the application becomes abandoned for failure to reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For replacement drawing handling see MPEP § 608.02(h). Use of form paragraphs and explicit deadlines (two months, three months at allowability) is required; extensions limited by statute (max six months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application not placed on files for examination until drawing objections corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility or plant application will not be placed on the files for examination until objections to the drawings have been corrected (37 CFR 1.85(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in § 1.215(c), any patent application publication will not include drawings filed after the application has been placed on the files for examination. Requests to hold drawing objections in abeyance are generally not considered bona fide attempts to advance the application (37 CFR 1.135(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected drawings must be newly submitted; Office will not release originals for correction
rubrics_metrics.description: If corrections are necessary, new corrected drawings must be submitted within the Office-set time; the Office will not release drawings for correction (37 CFR 1.85(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended replacement drawing sheets must be labeled 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' in the top margin per 37 CFR 1.121(d) and 1.84(c). If changes are not accepted, applicant will be notified in the next Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month period to file corrected drawing at allowability (nonextendable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a corrected drawing is required or an amended drawing does not comply when an application is allowed, the Office may set a three-month period from the notice of allowability to file a corrected drawing; this period is not extendable under 1.136 (see 1.136(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file corrected drawings within this nonextendable period can result in abandonment. Be careful submitting replacement drawings after allowance because they will not normally be reviewed by an examiner and must not introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must show every feature of the invention specified in the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.83(a): The drawing in a nonprovisional application must show every feature of the invention specified in the claims; conventional features not essential to understanding may be illustrated with graphical symbols or labeled representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables and sequence listings included in the specification should not be duplicated in the drawings. Any structural detail essential for a proper understanding should be shown. If the invention is an improvement on an old machine, show the improved portion disconnected from the old structure and also another view showing connection (37 CFR 1.83(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require additional illustration when drawings noncompliant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where drawings do not comply with 1.83(a) and (b), the examiner shall require such additional illustration within a period of not less than two months from the notice (subject to 1.81(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections requested are subject to 37 CFR 1.81(d). Form paragraphs (e.g., 6.22.01, 6.22.04) may be used to require illustration. Failure to provide will subject the application to the usual consequences (abandonment if not timely).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement drawing sheet content and labeling rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amended replacement drawing sheet should include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet (even if only one figure is amended); do not label amended figure as 'amended'. If a figure is canceled, remove it and renumber remaining figures and update the brief description of the several views for consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional replacement sheets may be necessary to show renumbering. Each drawing sheet submitted after filing must be labeled 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' in the top margin pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to employ competent draftsperson (form paragraph 6.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: New corrected drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required; applicant is advised to employ a competent patent draftsperson outside the Office as the USPTO does not prepare new drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected drawings required in reply to Office action to avoid abandonment; requirement will not be held in abeyance. Examiner may insert specific reason for objection in bracket 1 of the form paragraph (e.g., drawings do not show every feature of the claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period for replacement drawings when drawings prevent examination (form paragraph 6.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: When drawings are not of sufficient quality to permit examination, replacement drawing sheets are required and applicant is given a shortened statutory period of TWO (2) MONTHS to submit new drawings (extensions may be obtained under 1.136(a) but cannot carry reply beyond the statutory six-month maximum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of this paragraph should be rare and limited to instances where no examination can be performed due to poor drawing quality. Failure to timely submit replacement sheets will result in abandonment. Use PTOL-90 or PTO-90C as cover sheet for such communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for marked-up (annotated) copy of corrected drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to replacement sheets containing corrected figures, applicant is required to submit a marked-up copy of each replacement sheet including annotations indicating the changes made; the marked-up copy must be labeled 'Annotated Sheet' and included in the amendment or remarks section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.121(d)(1) and (d)(2). Failure to timely submit corrected drawing and marked-up copy will result in abandonment. Examiners may require the marked-up copy via form paragraph (e.g., 6.27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage submission of corrected drawings before allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be encouraged to submit corrected drawings before allowance to avoid having any term adjustment reduced pursuant to 37 CFR 1.704(c)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting corrections pre-allowance avoids last-minute issues and nonextendable deadlines at allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of replacement drawings after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If replacement drawings are filed after allowance, each sheet should include application number and art unit in the upper center margin (37 CFR 1.84(c)) and be labeled 'Replacement Sheet'. In utility applications, examination will normally be conducted using the originally presented drawings; replacement drawings after allowance will not normally be reviewed by an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is applicant's responsibility to ensure no new matter is added when submitting replacement drawings after allowance. If the examiner notices new matter, appropriate action should be taken to have the new matter deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage and format rules for drawings and photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Black-and-white line drawings in provisional, nonprovisional, PCT/national stage, and reexamination proceedings will be converted to TIFF images and stored in IFW; various categories (B&W photos, grayscale, color) will be stored in a content management system with a black-and-white copy placed in the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings and photographs are not permitted in international applications (PCT Rule 11.13). Originally submitted color paper drawings/photographs may be maintained in an artifact folder. Design and reissue design drawings may be handled slightly differently (content management system + placeholder sheet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must not duplicate tables or sequence listings from the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables included in the specification and sequences in sequence listings should not be duplicated in the drawings (37 CFR 1.83(a) and 1.58(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundancy between specification and drawings; follow citation rules for sequence listings and tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete illustration obligation — show structural details of importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any structural detail that is of sufficient importance to be described should be shown in the drawing. (Ex parte Good, 1911.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs (6.22.01, 6.22.04, 6.36) to require illustration when essential structural details are missing. If a feature is claimed but not shown, the feature must be shown or cancelled from the claim(s); no new matter should be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must ensure completeness and consistency of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should ensure figures are correctly described in the brief description of the several views, reference characters are properly applied, no single reference character is used for two different parts or for a part and its modification, and there are no superfluous illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate form paragraphs to require correction. Specific form paragraphs (6.22.02, 6.22.03, 6.22.06, 6.22.07) address mismatches between reference numerals in drawings and specification and require corrected sheets or specification amendments per 37 CFR 1.121(d) and 1.121(b). Objections will not be held in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for reference characters consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must not use different numbers to refer to the same part, nor use the same number for different parts; drawings must include all reference signs mentioned in the description and must not include reference signs not mentioned in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reference numbers are missing from drawings, require corrected drawing sheets; if drawings include reference characters not in the description, require either corrected drawing sheets or amendment to the specification to add the reference characters in the description (37 CFR 1.121(d) or 1.121(b)). Use form paragraphs 6.22.02, 6.22.03, 6.22.06, 6.22.07 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications must be illustrated or text canceled
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications may not be shown in broken lines on figures which show in solid lines another form of the invention; all modifications described must be illustrated or the text canceled (Ex parte Badger; Ex parte Peck).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement does not apply to mere reference to minor variations or well-known/conventional parts. Use form paragraph 6.22.05 to require correction when modified forms are shown improperly in the same view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art figures generally unnecessary and should be labeled 'Prior Art' if retained
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures showing the prior art are usually unnecessary and should be canceled; where needed to understand the invention they may be retained if designated by a legend such as 'Prior Art'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art figure is not labeled, use form paragraph 6.36.01 to require designation and corrected drawings as necessary.
